segments.text: Atascha, Chidepi, Naisarike, Pranam Sambande, yes, Tazarudha, Antrim Kalam, Mimarashtra,
Nastya, Sir, Lokotareva.
So Chidepi, Naisarike, Pranam Sambande, although he is breathing in and out, just like
us.
But actually, yes, Tazarudha, Antrim Kalam, Mimarashtra, the one, that yogi, who is always
aware of that supreme state of internal being of consciousness, in breathing also, so Lokotareva
is beyond the state of ordinary people, he is allowed to take.
Naisika, Antar, Madhya, Samyamath, Kematra, Savya, Upasavya, Savshamni issue, the one who
is centered, whose consciousness is centralized in Naisika, in Madhya, in central vein, all
in that Pranam, the state of Pranam, whose consciousness is centralized, centralized in that
breath, in that central vein, Pranam, Pranam, Pranam, this is not Kundalini, this is the
force of Kundalini, the one who is attached to that force, Kematra, Savya, Savshamni issue,
not to him, if he travels in Pranam, if he travels in Apana, if he travels in Sushamna,
what to him, he is always the same, Kematra, Savya, Upasavya, Savshamni issue, for him, there
is no difference, he may travel in ordinary breathing, he may travel in that Pranam, Shakti, or
he may travel in Madhya, in central vein, this is one and the same thing for him, Sarvonadi,
Chakra Pradhanur, Upasavya, Savshamni issue, the right vein, the left vein and the central
vein, which is predominant in all veins, all 72,000 veins, predominant veins are only three,
Yura, Pingala, and Sushamna, that is the Chennaadi, Vamanadi and Madhya-Nadi, Naseka, Naseka means
Nasete, Kautilena, Vaheti, Idhikrta, Kutil Vahini, Pranashati, that energy of breath, that energy
of breath that gives life and that removes the stiffness in your body, this gets stiff just when you
leave this physical frame, this will get stiff, you can't fold it, you can't fold this, you can't
fold any part, any limb of your body at that moment, because that Pranashati is gone, Tasha
Anthar, and whose consciousness is centralized in the center of that, Anthiri Sambhya, that internal
consciousness, Tasha Abhimadhyam, and in the center of that true Sarvantara-Tamataya Pradhanam,
which is predominant in each and every being of everything, Tasha Abhimadhyam Pranam, Madhyam Pranam in
whole of the body. Tasha Deva, Deva, Parabhova, the Surupina, Yamarsha, Parama, Shakti, Sarvajag,
Janishya, Linga, for that who is Lord of Lords, who is one with Supreme cognition, Parabhova,
the Surupina, his Supreme energy is only awareness, energy of awareness, which is all knowing and all
acting, and all glorious, which Rikali Kramavaktinitya, Yath, Yumarsha, Mayam, Rupam, that the
formation of that awareness, Tasha Samyamarth, when you put your consciousness to that awareness,
what is putting that? What is meant by putting your consciousness in that awareness? That is
under Nivalanaprakashya, but be aware in continuity of your being.
Then what to say to him? I am he, Sarvadashya, Dedi, Pimano, Nirvithana, Parasamari. This person
is centralized and glorified with that Supreme Samyadi, which is why there is no Vithana for him.
Saduktam tree, Vigyanabhairava, Grahya, Grahya, this is said in Vigyanabhairava also,
Grahya, Grahya, Grahya, Sambhiti, Samaanya, Sarvadeh Nam, Yoginam, Tvisheshoyam, Sambandeya,
Sahaja, Sahaja. This knowledge of objective knowledge and cognitive knowledge,
no, subject to knowledge, subject to knowledge and objective knowledge is same in every being,
in each and every being, living being. But to Yogis only there is one difference that in
the connection of these cognitive knowledge and subject to knowledge, subject to knowledge
in connection with these two, they are aware. This is the difference between Yogis and
the ordinary person. Best, should we do it?
